$comment: The scope object of spec §13j. Set by the field's experts, not by the agent and not by the owner. Versioned: a change here is a change to what the agent may work on. This field is declared AHEAD of its agent: no brain-recording corpus exists on this machine, and a field whose answer key is absent cannot be scored — see human-brain-llm.md.
$agent_id_comment: null: no agent exists for this field yet — research_agents.registry knows seven names and this is not one. A field declared ahead of its agent is a draft, and the console shows it as one. Promotion requires a corpus with held-out subjects and a judge that the proposing role does not own.
principle: shared structure between a language model and a brain must be measured against what the STIMULUS ALONE predicts; an encoding score a stimulus-only or size-matched control also reaches is not evidence of shared computation — stated so it can be wrong, and it very often is

set_by.$comment: roles, never names — naming a person in a design document commits them to something they have not agreed to. `named` is filled when a panel exists.

in.subfield: encoding models — predicting recorded neural responses from model representations
in.boundary: always reported beside a stimulus-only floor (word rate, surprisal, acoustic and low-level features) and a size-matched control model

in.subfield: decoding — recovering stimulus properties from recordings
in.boundary: reported with the identification baseline and with subject-disjoint splits; a within-subject split reads the subject, not the language
normalised by an explicitly estimated noise ceiling, with the ceiling reported and not folded into the number

in.subfield: generalisation across subjects, sessions and datasets
in.boundary: held-out subjects and held-out recordings; a result that does not survive a new subject is a result about that subject

in.subfield: re-validation of published brain-score and alignment claims
in.boundary: against the stimulus-only floor those claims were mostly never asked to clear

out.question: whether a model understands, is conscious, or has experience
out.why: no recording is an answer key for it; a benchmark that scored it would be scoring a definition, not a fact

out.question: any clinical or diagnostic statement about a named individual
out.why: this agent may say what predicts group-level response; it may never say anything about a person

out.question: advocacy for a model architecture
out.why: a field that both proposes an architecture and rules on its brain-likeness has replaced validation with authorship

out.question: mechanism in neural tissue — why a population responds
out.why: correlational recordings cannot score it; it needs intervention and a different answer key

out.question: collecting the recordings
out.why: scanner and electrode time is the binding constraint, and consent is held by a person, never by an agent

adjacent.relation: shares the inverse-problem machinery for reconstructing fMRI and MEG; owns the reconstruction, not the interpretation
owns acquisition physics and artefact behaviour of the scanners this field reads from
owns the cohorts, the consent, the stimulus design and any causal claim

claims_allowed: what a model representation adds over a stimulus-only floor, on held-out subjects it was not fitted on
noise-ceiling-normalised similarity with the ceiling reported beside it
that a representation adds nothing over the floor, which is the expected answer most of the time
claims_forbidden: any claim about understanding, consciousness or experience
any claim about a named individual
an encoding or alignment score reported without the stimulus-only floor and the noise ceiling beside it
a claim of brain-likeness supported only by a correlation that a larger model also achieves
would_move_the_boundary: the question becoming CAUSAL — whether perturbing a representation changes the neural response. No correlational recording can score that, so it is a different twin and a different answer key. The response is fission, not a wider scope
$watch_comment: if the stimulus-only floor stays unbeaten across every candidate representation, the field's own principle has been confirmed in its least flattering direction, and the experts decide whether that is a finding or a closure (§13j).
